rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.10 describe a two-factor pot experiment (drip vs flood irrigation x 18/24/30 <U+00B0>C soil temperature, four replicates) with the authors' own measurements of photosynthesis, enzymes, hormones, pollen viability and yield. Q2: Table 1 and Section 3.1 report that Pn, Gs, Ci and Tr were 15, 31, 9 and 16% lower under DI than FI, including at 30 <U+00B0>C (Discussion: at T3 DI reduced photosynthetic performance relative to FI); Sections 3.2-3.7, Figs 2-5, Tables 2-3 and the Abstract/Conclusion report that the negative effects of low soil temperature (18 and 24 <U+00B0>C) on MDA, proline, hormones, pollen viability, spikelets and yield were greater under DI than FI. Q4: the study measures intermediate variables linking irrigation method to yield loss: leaf gas exchange (Table 1), antioxidant enzymes, MDA and proline as stress markers (Figs 2-3), spikelet hormones (Fig 4), pollen viability (Fig 5) and surviving branches/spikelets (Table 2). Q9: Figs 2-5 report error bars as SE (n = 3) for protein, enzyme, MDA, proline, hormone and pollen-viability results.
rows.notes: Q3: the result rests on one pot experiment; different measured variables (gas exchange, biochemical assays, yield) are not independent methods establishing the same result, so rated no. Q7: the authors state that low soil temperature/cold water aggravates drip-irrigation stress and that the problem could be avoided by warming irrigation water (Conclusion), and that 90-95% FC is a mild stress environment for cultivar T-43; this is close to a stated condition but is presented as an interaction/suggestion, so conservatively rated no. Q8: no limitations of the pot-scale, single-soil, single-cultivar, 10-day temperature treatment design are stated. Q9: SE given only in figures; Table 1 (photosynthesis) and Table 3 (yield) give letter groupings and F values without dispersion measures.

notes: Full text available. Pot experiment with one sandy loam soil, one rice cultivar (T-43), soil-temperature treatments applied for 10 days at panicle initiation; statistics by Duncan's test and two-way ANOVA.
